purpose: Methimazole is used to treat an overactive thyroid gland, a condition called hyperthyroidism. It helps bring your thyroid hormone levels back to normal. It can also be used to prepare patients for thyroid surgery or radioactive iodine treatment.
how_it_works: Your thyroid gland makes hormones that control your body's energy and metabolism. When your thyroid makes too much hormone, it can cause symptoms like rapid heartbeat, weight loss, and anxiety. Methimazole works by blocking your thyroid gland from producing too much of these hormones, helping your body get back into balance.
common_side_effects: Some common side effects include nausea, upset stomach, headache, dizziness, mild skin rash or itching, and joint pain. Some people may also notice changes in their sense of taste. These effects are often mild and may go away as your body adjusts to the medication.
warnings: Important warning: In rare cases, methimazole can cause a serious drop in white blood cells, which fight infection. Call your doctor right away if you develop a fever, sore throat, mouth sores, or unusual infections. It can also rarely cause liver problems, so contact your doctor if you notice yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain. This medication should NOT be used during pregnancy, especially the first trimester, as it can harm the baby.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose for adults is 15 to 60 mg per day, divided into doses taken every 6 to 8 hours. Once your thyroid levels are under control, your doctor will likely lower your dose to a smaller maintenance amount, often 5 to 15 mg per day. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes and try to take it at the same times each day.
